newsitem.title: USA: US blue chips end lower, profit-taking hits techs.
newsitem.headline: US blue chips end lower, profit-taking hits techs.

text.p: The Dow industrials posted modest losses on Thursday after a session dominated by profit-taking, particularly among large-cap technology stocks.

The Dow fell 27 points to close unofficially at 7330. The blue-chip average was led lower by International Business Machines Corp, which fell 2-1/4 to 87-7/8. Shares in computer networkers slumped after striking big gains recently.
"A lot of these tech stocks had made ferocious runs in a very volatile market," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.
"Wall Street always tends to go to extremes, and there's always a snapback afterwards," he said.
Among networking stocks, 3Com Corp fell 3-5/16 to 47-13/16 after rallying nearly 10 points in the past week alone. Ascend Communications Inc slipped 2-3/4 to 56-5/8 after a similar run.

With many major indices near their all-time highs, analysts said they detected an increased sense of caution in the market. Several key economic reports are due over the next week, which also likely prodded some investors to tuck away gains won during a six-week market surge, they said.
"We have a couple of pieces of data coming up that are going to be very important," said Philip Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management.
Among the closest watched of the upcoming reports are monthly job and wage figures as well as the National Association of Purchasing Management index, due next week.

Due tomorrow is a revised look at first-quarter Gross Domestic Product (GDP). While that report is somewhat dated by market standards, it is sure to draw attention because of the breathtaking pace of economic growth it is expected to show.
Forecasts are for a revised real GDP growth rate of 6.0 percent, up from the 5.6 percent rate in the preliminary report, according to economists surveyed by Reuters.
Some analysts wonder if even the forecasts, which are more than double the growth rate the Federal Reserve is believed to target, are high enough.

"We think the potential exists for a positive surprise there and that second-quarter GDP could also come in above current expectations," Orlando said. "All that suggests the Fed erred by not tightening" at its last interest rate policy meeting earlier this month.

Such worries failed to emerge in the bond market, however, which turned in a solid performance. Yields on the long bond dipped below the key seven percent level, settling at 6.98 percent in late afternoon activity, though the bond market's gains failed to spark a rally for financial stocks.
Personal computer makers showed steep losses after unfavorable comments by several analysts.

Early in the day, Salomon Brothers lowered its rating on IBM to buy from strong buy, helping spur the broad decline in the group. Gateway 2000 Inc tumbled 5-7/8 to 68-1/2 and Compaq Computer Corp fell five to 101-3/4.

Nike Inc skidded 8-5/8 to 55-3/8. The athletic footwear maker warned Thursday its fourth-quarter earnings would fall short of Wall Street estimates, a development that wiped out two days of gains that are largely driven by rumors.
"If you're buying on rumors, sometimes you get hurt," said Doug Meyers, vice president of equity trading at Interstate/Johnson Lane.

Gucci Group NV fell 5-7/8 to 68-1/2. The luxury goods company told analysts its sales in April were hurt by a weak yen, which limited buying in Japanese markets. Analysts said Gucci warned the trend may have extended into this month.
The S&P 500 fell 3.13 points to 844.08.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 7.14 points to 1403.04.
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1881))
